source: On the day that Bleu was available, 27% of the adoptable dogs in Washington came into the local rescues and shelters from out of state.
why: With these files Washington has 1,277 adoptable dogs, not the 1,265 in the text, and 334 of them (26.2%, which rounds to 26%) have an out-of-state origin, so neither the count nor the 27% share reproduces.

source: But Washington is one of only 13 states that didn't import adoptable dogs from other states or countries.
why: Washington has 334 dogs with an out-of-state origin in the data; the 13 states with no imports are Alaska, Hawaii, Idaho, Louisiana, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, New Mexico, North Dakota, South Dakota, Texas, West Virginia and Wyoming.

source: In fact, Washington exported 55 adoptable pups to other states.
why: Only 2 dogs originating in Washington are listed for adoption in another state, and the story's own export chart lists Washington with 2, not 55.

source: I looked at the PetFinder profiles of all 58,000 dogs available for adoption across the US on a single day and found 2,460 dogs whose travel was described in enough detail to follow.
why: A count of records in the analytic subset (the travel file yields exactly 2,460 imported dogs), i.e. a description of the data rather than a finding; the number is used as a denominator in the claims.

source: In all, over 3,000 dogs were described as having originated in places different from where they were listed for adoption.
why: A count of records (3,269 distinct dogs in the travel file have an origin different from their listing state), i.e. a description of the data rather than a finding.

source: Using the PetFinder API, details about all 58,180 dogs available for adoption in the 50 US states and Washington DC on September 20, 2019 were collected.
why: The size of the dataset (the descriptions file has 58,180 rows), not a finding.

source: In 2018, the ASPCA reports that they relocated over 40,000 animals from areas of “high homeless pet overpopulation” to “areas with a higher demand for adoptable dogs”.
why: Cited from an external ASPCA report, not computed from these files.

source: An estimated 250,000 animals were left behind. Around 15,000 of those animals were saved during the aftermath of the storm by Louisiana’s SPCA and other rescue organizations from across the country.
why: Historical figures cited from external sources, not computed from these files.

source: A 2017 study estimates that out of the 5.5 million dogs brought into shelters in the US annually, 780,000 (15%) are euthanized.
why: External study estimate, not computed from these files.

source: Heartworm rates in Seattle-dwelling dogs have skyrocketed over 300% between 2012 and 2017.
why: External statistic reported by SeattleDogSpot, not computed from these files.

source: After Rhode Island’s incidence rate for the deadly (and contagious) canine parvovirus went from two incidents per year to two per week in 2012, they have a right to be worried.
why: External statistic cited from a news report, not computed from these files.
